findings.description: The check says to run the reproduction "verbatim" and then requires that "both invocations must exit nonzero", but the verbatim reproduction at spec.md:38-40 prints no exit status and a shell block surfaces only the last command's code, so the exit-code half of the check is not observable without modifying the reproduction the check just told the checker not to modify; the link-broken half was re-derived live and behaves as claimed (v1 scope failures: 0, v2 scope prints link-broken).

"$S/v2"` / `rm -rf "$S"` with no `echo $?`. Live run on 59c363f: v1 'failures: 0' exit=0, v2 'FAIL .../2026-02-03-atlas-dry-run-prep-zFpm-hfD5u.md: link-broken' exit=1.

findings.description: The text's last claim — that a v1 file "contributes nothing to the scope-wide open-slug set that feeds that loop and the RECURRING report" — is invisible to the check, verified by simulating an implementation that feeds v1 bodies into `$work/open-slugs`: it passes C-3's check (failures: 0, exit=0) and passes C-4 (diff=0 across all ten scopes) while silently suppressing a real `open-question-resolution` failure on a v2 note, so text and check return opposite verdicts on one artifact.
findings.evidence: Simulated impl appending `extract_body "$file" | grep -oE -- '\[open question: [^]]*\]' | sed ... >>"$work/open-slugs"` at lint-scope.sh:418. C-3 check output: 'failures: 0 / exit=0'. C-4 check output: 'diff=0'. On a mixed scope with the slug opened in a v1 note and resolved in a v2 note: stock 'failures: 2' with the open-question-resolution FAIL, simulated impl 'failures: 1' with the FAIL gone.

findings.description: PASS, and the strongest clause in the document: the verbatim `git worktree add -q --detach "$BASE" HEAD` into an existing empty `mktemp -d` works on this git, the comparison prints diff=0 today, the non-goal against committing keeps HEAD equal to the pre-fix tree, it stays diff=0 against a simulated correct fix, and it catches the named wrong implementation loudly on both the count lines and the failures lines.

findings.description: The parenthetical cites `.gitignore:5-7` for the guild-state ignore, but lines 5-6 are the tail of a comment and the rule spans lines 7-8 (`.agent-guild/state/*` plus its `!.agent-guild/state/archive/` negation), so the citation range is off by one on each end.
findings.evidence: .gitignore:5-6 are '# carrying, so they travel while the working state stays local.' continuation lines; :7 is '.agent-guild/state/*'; :8 is '!.agent-guild/state/archive/'.

findings.description: The check is unsatisfiable without work the non-goals forbid: it demands that "the last `EXIT` trap in the file lists every `mktemp -d` path the file creates", but the last trap at :1203 omits two of the file's eighteen scratch paths — `$overrun_scope` (created :195, dropped by the trap at :239) and `$tpl_scope` (created :345, dropped by the trap at :625) — so a worker who satisfies the clause's text exactly (each new trap carrying every path from the trap before it) still fails its check, and the only way to pass is to edit pre-existing traps.
findings.evidence: tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh: 18 `mktemp -d` assignments at :195,238,273,292,345,624,745,776,779,800,841,894,956,1013,1090,1118,1176,1202. Final trap :1203 lists 16 names, missing `$overrun_scope` and `$tpl_scope`. Trap :239 is `trap 'rm -rf "$not_a_scope" "$inline_scope"' EXIT` (overrun dropped); trap :625 is `... "$dismissal_scope" "$mig"' EXIT` (tpl dropped).

findings.description: The non-goal's exemption is aimed at the wrong line: #30's break at :293 is self-healing because the trap at :346 re-lists `$inline_scope` and `$dismissal_scope`, so :293 is not what makes the check unsatisfiable, and the constitution's assurance that C-7 "does not ask anyone to repair the existing break" is true of :293 and false of the two drops that actually bite.
findings.evidence: tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:293 `trap 'rm -rf "$not_a_scope"' EXIT` vs :346 `trap 'rm -rf "$not_a_scope" "$inline_scope" "$dismissal_scope" "$tpl_scope"' EXIT`. constitution.md:136 names only :293.

findings.description: The check's only stated fail trigger sits one notch off its text: the text requires each of the four sentences to "describe the code as shipped", but the check fails a location only when its "sentence cannot be tied to a line", so a rewrite that is confidently tie-able and factually wrong (say, :10-12 recast as "every v1 file is checked for tokens", tied to :444-445, which makes it false) satisfies the check and violates the text.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:107 text ('each must describe the code as shipped') vs. constitution.md:108 check ('A location whose sentence cannot be tied to a line fails.'). All four cited locations resolve: lint-scope.sh:10-12, :441-443, references/machine-contracts.md:7, SKILL.md:428.

findings.description: The clause contradicts itself and is jointly unsatisfiable with C-1: its first sentence grants that files with no `schema` key now reach `check_links`, and its third sentence forbids that "no check newly applies to a v1 file", which is precisely the change C-1 makes mandatory, so read literally no artifact can satisfy both C-1 and C-9.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:114 — 'The only behavioral change is that files with no `schema` key now reach `check_links`. ... and no check newly applies to a v1 file.' against constitution.md:20 — '`lint-scope.sh` prints a `link-broken` line naming that note ... The file's schema generation has no bearing on the outcome.'

findings.description: The text requires each rewritten passage to survive "the `humanizer` skill's audit" but the check never invokes the humanizer and instead applies an unrelated two-part rubric (reason attached to rule, register matching the surrounding file), so a passage can pass the check and violate the text, and the checker is given no way to see the half of the text it is not asked to test.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:121 text names the humanizer; constitution.md:122 check reads 'read each rewritten passage against the three or four paragraphs around it and name any sentence that states a rule with no reason attached, or that reads in a register the surrounding file does not use.' The skill itself exists at ~/.claude/skills/humanizer, so the citation resolves; the check simply does not exercise it.

findings.description: On the orchestrator's specific question, the C-2/C-3 versus C-1/C-4 division is sound and leaves no way to satisfy the constitution without fixing anything: C-2 and C-3 do pass vacuously on the unfixed tree, but C-1 cannot, because the reproduction's v1 scope prints 'failures: 0' until v1 files reach check_links, and a simulated correct fix flips it to a link-broken line with exit 1.
findings.evidence: Unfixed 59c363f: v1 scope 'v1 files: 4 / failures: 0', exit=0. Simulated fix (v1_files array plus a link-only pass): 'FAIL .../2025-11-04-atlas-scoping-call-3iMu15QJ_x.md: link-broken', 'failures: 1', 'v1 exit=1'.

findings.description: Coverage is complete: all six of the spec's Acceptance Criteria map to at least one clause (AC1 to C-1, AC2 to C-2, AC3 to C-3, AC4 to C-4, AC5 to C-5, AC6 to C-8), and both of the interview's out-of-issue scope decisions are covered too (the three extra prose locations by C-8, the durable regression coverage by C-7), so no acceptance criterion is orphaned.
